extracted.intended_audience: creative writing teachers, writing studies researchers, and L2 writing instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Quantitative measurement of engagement and emotional tone in second-language (L2) creative-writing tasks, comparing autobiographical prompts with critical consciousness-raising prompts using surveys and computational text analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative-writing engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall measure of writers' engagement while producing narrative creative writing; reported as higher for autobiographical creative writing (M = 5.35, SD = 1.09) than for critical consciousness-raising creative writing (M = 4.59, SD = 1.16), t(29) = 3.18, p = .003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via survey instruments administered to L2 writers; treated as an aggregate engagement score for each prompt type. Statistical comparisons (means, SDs, t-tests) used to determine significant differences between prompt conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attentional focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reported measure of the writer's ability to focus attention while writing; writers reported significantly more attentional focus while writing in response to an autobiographical prompt (p = .015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a subcomponent of narrative-writing engagement; higher attentional focus indicates deeper immersion in the writing task. Typically measured by questionnaire items assessing concentration and distraction during writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative presence
rubrics_metrics.description: The feeling of 'being there' in the world the writer was creating (i.e., sense of presence within the narrative); writers reported significantly greater narrative presence while responding to autobiographical prompts (p = .047).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a distinct engagement subdimension and measured by self-report items. Higher narrative presence signals stronger immersive narrative experience and relates to both engagement and emotional involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reported degree of emotional involvement while writing; writers who reported enjoying creative writing in English the most also reported significantly more emotional engagement while writing autobiographical pieces (p = .033).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via survey; can be moderated by individual differences such as reported enjoyment of the writing activity. Note: overall, emotional engagement did not differ significantly between autobiographical and critical consciousness-raising prompts at the group level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional tone (text-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: The valence of emotion expressed in the written text as measured by computational-linguistic/text analysis; the autobiographical prompt elicited a significantly more positive emotional tone (p < .001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from computational-linguistic analysis of short stories (text output), rather than self-report. Useful for triangulating self-reported emotional engagement with objective textual indicators of positive/negative affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reported enjoyment of creative writing in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers' reported enjoyment level of creative writing in English used as an individual-difference predictor; higher enjoyment was associated with greater emotional engagement and narrative presence when writing autobiographical pieces (emotional engagement p = .033; narrative presence p = .01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as a moderator variable in analyses; grouping by enjoyment level can reveal differential responses to prompt types. Measured via survey items asking about enjoyment levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt type (autobiographical vs. critical consciousness-raising)
rubrics_metrics.description: The genre/stance of the writing prompt (autobiographical personal-response prompt versus critical consciousness-raising prompt) which influences engagement and emotional tone outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary experimental condition/comparison in the study. Choosing prompt type is a pedagogical decision that can systematically affect attentional focus, narrative presence, emotional engagement, and textual emotional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed-methods measurement approach (survey + text analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of statistical survey measures together with computational-linguistic analysis of short story texts to evaluate engagement and emotional tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining self-report and objective text analysis provides converging evidence; statistical testing used to assess significance of differences between conditions. This methodological rubric implies that robust measurement of writing engagement benefits from both subjective and textual indicators.
